issues.title: Customisable Collaborative Working
issues.body:
We have two current styles of Collaborative Working:
* Collaborative Editing
* Collaborative Responding

These support two separate business processes as documented [here](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1riB8Qazu34rWeRP6MEHi55jHvIfKr-LyWTkIYmfZ_gw/edit?usp=sharing)

The two approaches are hard-coded in Serge, with settings for the available verbs, which is the first (default) state, etc. So, the game designer chooses to add either a "Collaborative Editing" or "Collaborative Responding" when adding a new channel.

A more flexible strategy would be for the Game Designer to add a "Collaborative" channel, then offer extra UI features to edit the collaborative aspects not found in normal channels.

Should probably include these steps
* [x] Capture the settings currently hard-coded in Serge
* [x] Consider other ways in which a collaborative channel could be customised/tuned
* [x] Produce [data model](https://github.com/serge-web/serge/pull/1220/files#diff-23474f7ad9b79fea50d456796b02cd7e29ba0b3aa953cef1f913c24bda7d5569) for new channel designs
* [x] Produce UX for the new admin controls
* [x] #1278
* [x] Update display of controls in UI.  Ian suggests switching to a state table, to provide version of [this table](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1riB8Qazu34rWeRP6MEHi55jHvIfKr-LyWTkIYmfZ_gw/edit#slide=id.g10135b3f3a4_0_6) that is easier to read than complex if structure.


State table implemented [here](https://github.com/serge-web/serge/pull/1220/files#diff-ee67519811d145d751b631fdceecd304f8b77a3218620ef308dde7fc7dce4f36R35)

Hi - thanks for this work :-)

* [ ] For the force/role entries, we need the two toggles in each row. One is for 'Can submit' and the other is for 'Can see live updates'
* [ ] the 'edit/delete' pair of icons relates to the forces/roles, but not the "channel properties".  For the "channel properties", the controls should all be editable - with changes stored via a "Save" button for this channel (like in the "Overview" panel).
* [ ]  there is a _little_ logic in putting two template controls next to each other - though we should indicate that the response is editable
* [ ] for `initial document status` I propose a pair of radio buttons
* [ ] For the template lists, we should let the GD extend the list of templates. See the behaviour for `10. Dropdown` [here](https://careerfoundry.com/en/blog/ui-design/ui-element-glossary/). The benefit of this strategy is that the list of templates is visible.
* [ ] For the list of verbs, we should have a list control where new items get added at the bottom. Maybe leave some flexibility in the design for this - and let the devs find a suitable control.
* [ ] `Terminology` - yes, a good decision to try to organise this content.
* [ ] Hopefully we can come up with a more compact layout - so the GD can see the properties at the top, and then the list of participants.

Like the video, nice work @lebaphi 

**Templates**.  For `Message Template` and `Response Template` only one template can be selected from the drop-down list.

**Approve/Release/Request-Changes**. For these lists, the player needs to be able to add any word.  They are entering the _verb_ to be used when describing the action. e.g. `Request changes` could be used by a number of different business processes, so we need to let the Game. Designer enter a verb that relates to the business process he is supporting.  Note: the lists will start off with a single value in each list - to help the Game Designer understand how things work. But, the Game Designer can delete any of these items, and even leave a list empty (if that type of action isn't required).

**Additional fields**.  The player will need to be able to add free-text terms to this list. This will (probably) be the id of a field in the template, and we don't know what the fields will be.  So, any word can be added.

**Mapping**. We still have to design the UI for the mapping admin page. So, for now, just create a _Standard_ channel page (with just the list of roles).
